chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Goldberg's Texas bookings and the decision to go east
summary: The booker could only book Texas; Whiteman's remark that they were too good for a regional band pushes them toward St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Goldberg was booking you through Texas, but does he book you after you go out of Texas?
No, not after we left Texas.
In other words, he couldn't do anything but book you in Texas?
What made you want to-- obviously you all wanted to be bigger than just a Texas band; right?

Paul Whiteman came up with the statement that the band was much too good to be identified as a local band, a local Texas band. It should be a national band, and that stuck in our minds and we started--I was one of the main ones to keep at them to go east, let's go east. That's
what we finally decided, we finally said le'ts go try it.
When we left there we went into St. Louis.
Is that the first place you went to after leaving Texas?
Well, it was one of the first places.
We made a tour all the way up to Little Rock and through Tennessee--
What was this, all one nighters?
